rv.q: This indie musical for kids deftly channels the freewheeling silliness of Dav Pilkey’s graphic novels.
The Dog Man books are chaotic, hilarious and full of pathos, but writer/lyricist Aguila and composer Brad Alexander’s show leans largely on the former.
Slick, intelligent attempt to stage Dav Pilkey’s super-successful graphic novels
The show is short (but performed across two acts) and silly – just as it should be.
Perhaps my main concern is whether Dog Man truly needs to be a musical.
However, if you’re just looking for some lo-fi family-friendly fun with a few good songs, I’d hold on for panto season.
No matter your age, Dog Man: The Musical is a perfect treat, hilarious and whimsical, crafty and smart.
If your child loves Dog Man books, they’ll love this too.
Based on four of Dav Pilkey’s immensely popular graphic Dog Man stories, this is a decent enough children’s musical (by Aguila and Brad Alexander) although it’s unremarkable.

cn.t: Critics find this adaptation of Dav Pilkey's popular graphic novels captures the books' chaotic silliness and delights young fans, though some deem it unremarkable beyond its primary school-aged target audience.
